newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW-ITT sees Hilton bid as helpful.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-ITT sees Hilton bid as helpful.

text.p: A $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid by Hilton Hotels Corp for ITT Corp has strengthened ITT, which hopes to get leaner and raise shareholder value to avoid a takeover, an ITT official said on Wednesday.
"In a sense it had a very positive impact," said Daniel Weadock, senior vice-president of ITT and chief executive of the company's wholly-owned hotel group, ITT Sheraton Corp.

"We had a long-term plan to be implemented over a 3-1/2 to four year period. Long term became nine months, once Hilton announced the takeover plan," Weadock told Reuters in an interview during a visit to Thailand.
ITT has been selling properties and assets it has deemed to be "non-core" to focus on the hotels and gaming businesses in an effort to thwart the hostile bid launched by Hilton in January.
Among the higher-profile assets sold by ITT were its 50 percent stake in New York's Madison Square Garden and a portion of its stake in French telecommunications company Alcatel Alsthom.
"There is concern with regard to our shareholders, when someone comes at you like this." said Weadock. "But fortunately we had a backup plan. We had a number of assets we could monetise."
Weadock said the company's goal is to increase ITT's share price and convince shareholders against a takeover by Hilton.
"You have to take this seriously. It's gotten us more focused," he said. "It's our objective to drive the price of the shares high through the actions we're taking with our non-core assets."
He said a realistic goal for the share price this year could be about $80.

ITT shares closed at $60-1/2 on Tuesday, and have been rising from about $42 before Hilton launched the offer. The stock has consistently traded above Hilton's bid on views that Hilton could raise its bid.
Hilton launched a $55-per-share cash and stock bid for ITT in late January. ITT rejected the bid, calling it inadequate.
In March analysts said ITT had to take aggressive actions to pacify restless investors.
Last week a federal appelate court in the United States denied an expedited hearing of Hilton's appeal of a lower court ruling in its takeover battle.

Hilton had asked a district court in Las Vegas, Nevada to compel ITT to hold its annual meeting in mid-May. Hilton has nominated a slate of directors to ITT's board in an attempt to unseat its current members.
A U.S. district judge denied Hilton's motion in April.
ITT has not yet set a date for the shareholder's meeting and has until late November to do so.
Weadock said he expected the meeting to take place between late October and mid-November.
He said shareholders would ultimately decide the fate of the company, but said since Hilton had announced its takeover bid it had accumulated less than one percent of the company's shares.
